name: Trigger file downloads
plain: Saves a file to the device; repeated automatic downloads ask permission.
meaning: A site can drop files into Downloads (reports, exports, installers). Browsers guard with multi-download prompts and safe browsing checks because a downloaded file is how malware arrives.

access.persistence: Chrome stores Automatic downloads permission per origin after the person allows it
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Sandboxed frames need allow-downloads (Chrome 83); downloads from cross-origin iframes without activation are blocked
steps: Page creates anchor or sends Content-Disposition
Safe Browsing may warn or block

limits.headline: Can save a file to your device, but repeated automatic downloads ask first
limits.user_action: Nothing for the first one. It happens when the page runs a download or you tap a link.
can: Save a file to your Downloads folder when you tap a download link
Make a file on the spot, such as a receipt or a report, and save it
Start one download without asking in most browsers
cannot: Save many files in a row without a second prompt asking you to allow it
Open or run the file for you; you still have to open it
Save the file anywhere except the browser's download location
Skip the browser's warning for risky file types
limits.reach_label: One file, then it asks again
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Firefox ask before several automatic downloads. Safari on iPhone shows a download button for each file.

story.what_it_is: A site can save a file to your device, and the browser asks if it keeps doing it.
story.for_you: You click a button and a file lands in your Downloads folder. If a page tries to download many files by itself, the browser asks whether to allow that.
story.for_makers: Makers build files in the page (a report, an image, an export) and hand them over with one click. It saves server work and lets apps feel like desktop programs.

use_cases.example: You hit Export on a spreadsheet web app and it makes the CSV file right inside your browser.
A design tool saves your finished artwork as a PNG or PDF straight from the page.
Your bank offers a statement as a PDF download for your tax records.
A browser game lets you download your save file so you can move it to another computer.
A malicious site tries to push a file you did not ask for, which is why browsers warn on repeated automatic downloads.
A web video editor renders your clip and downloads the MP4 when it is done.

technical_bounds: download attribute is ignored for cross-origin URLs (Chrome 65, Firefox); filename comes from the response then
Second and later downloads without a click trigger Chrome's Automatic downloads prompt (Firefox shows a similar download panel)
Chrome blocks downloads from sandboxed iframes without allow-downloads (Chrome 83) and insecure (HTTP) downloads on HTTPS pages (Chrome 86 to 88)
Cannot choose the download folder; cannot open the file; dangerous file types get a warning
Blob URLs and data: URIs for large files are limited by memory (Chrome about 2 GB single Blob); stream with FSA or Streams for bigger files

history.change: download attribute ignored for cross-origin URLs
Downloads in sandboxed iframes need allow-downloads
Mixed-content downloads blocked in phases (executables first in Chrome 88)

refs.label: Chrome download restrictions in sandboxed iframes
